output.summary: Runtime dry-run dogfood found replay and UX gaps.

approvedRows.question: Can runtime worktree dry-runs append trace-owned claims that replay cleanly and render the planned isolation?
approvedRows.currentState: Runtime claim parents could point at subrefs such as trace:<planning>#work:<id>, which made replay fail after a real claim append; runtime rendering also hid worktree reasons and commands.
approvedRows.desiredState: Runtime claims use replay-valid parent event ids, and Pi runtime results show required worktrees, reasons, branches, and dry-run commands before source-writing automation is enabled.
approvedRows.rationale: A dry-run gate must prove trace append safety and operator-visible isolation before any autonomous source writes.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users get safer supervised automation because runtime claims can be replayed after append.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers can inspect worktree dry-run branches and commands directly in Pi renderer output.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: Evidence supports this intention as valuable and safe to plan.
